name: OPEC+
summary: OPEC+, Day 241. No decision in the window; the seven meet on 1 Nov on December output. The IEA sees a deficit through year-end with diesel tight into 2027; OPEC cut its 2026 growth estimate. Saudi Arabia's export capacity is under Houthi fire and tracker estimates of its exports conflict by up to 2.6 mb/d; the UAE, outside OPEC since May, pumped a record in September. The cartel's spare capacity is irrelevant while the constraint is safe passage.

current.sept_2026: OPEC+ agreed to raise SEPTEMBER output by +188,000 bpd, COMPLETING the rollback of its 2023 voluntary cuts — a genuine supply addition that, with the Iran strike pause, drove Brent -7.1% to $83.71 / WTI below $80 on 3 Aug. A structural bearish driver: if the war re-escalates, the premium now builds on top of a market ADDING barrels, not the tight-inventory setup of mid-July.

recent_signals.headline: No member statement before 29 Nov found. IEA OMR due 13 Nov 14:30 IST (after this brief). OPEC+ October output rise cited by Reuters as weighing on 12-Nov prices.

OPEC MOMR (11 Nov): OPEC+ crude output 41.23 mb/d in October (+2.04 mb/d m/m; ~97% of February's 42.72 per Al Jazeera/Reuters arithmetic). Saudi Arabia told OPEC 10.563 mb/d (direct communication; 8.372 in September); one secondary-source figure ~9.19 mb/d (AA; single relay) — a 1.37 mb/d gap. Demand growth unchanged: +180 kb/d 2026, +2.55 mb/d 2027. Kpler (via Reuters): Middle East outages down to ~3.8 mb/d; Saudi and Iraqi output back to pre-war. Release minute not found; content bearish.

**NO SIGNAL; ARAMCO SEEKS ASIAN SHARE (5 Nov):** the $2 Asian OSP cut to ~−$7 (REPORTED) is consistent with share-seeking ahead of 29 Nov (inference). No October survey found. (intel SAU)
No OPEC+ signal since the 1-Nov hold; Aramco December OSPs not out. No Gulf supply event behind the 4-Nov oil fall. (intel SAU-A1/A6/A10)

OPEC+ (the seven) held on 1 Nov: 'maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026' (total 31.01 mb/d; Saudi 10.478, Russia 9.949, Iraq 4.431, Kuwait 2.676, Kazakhstan 1.628, Algeria 1.007, Oman 0.841) — third straight pause; no market effect (priced). Capacity review for 2027 baselines due mid-November; all 21 members meet 29 Nov. Rystad's Leon: 'Today's decision was the easy one'. (CONFIRMED; intel SAU-A1, MAC-A3)

The seven (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan, Oman) meet online Sun 1 Nov and are 'likely to keep their December oil output targets steady' (Reuters, three sources, 27 Oct; 'no final decision'). Gulf members pump 'well below their targets' (~25 mb/d in August, ~5 mb/d below February); the 2023 1.65 mb/d cut is fully unwound; ~2 mb/d layer runs to end-2026; 2027 baselines (capacity review) are the real agenda, full OPEC+ meets 29 Nov. Rystad: 'OPEC+ currently has very limited power over the physical oil market.' A hold is price-neutral: quotas don't bind members that cannot reach them. (REPORTED; intel SAU-A11, MAC-A5)

No OPEC+ meeting or decision 13–26 Oct; the seven meet 1 Nov on December output. IEA (14 Oct): 2026 demand −2.6 mb/d, deficit through year-end, diesel tight into 2027; OPEC (13 Oct) cut 2026 growth to ~0.2 mb/d; IEA members agreed to accelerate stock releases (15 Oct, '>20mb' of diesel). UAE (outside OPEC) record September output (>4.4 mb/d per IEA via aggregator). (REPORTED; intel SAU-A11, MAC-A3)

**OPEC+ (now seven: Saudi, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, Oman) held November targets on 4 Oct; Saudi target 10.5 mb/d vs ~7.4 mb/d actual (Kpler) — increases 'stayed on paper'.** Next meeting ~1 Nov (date not found); 2027 capacity review pending. UAE (outside OPEC) ~4.2 mb/d (+0.3 vs pre-war). No second departure. — CONFIRMED.

No OPEC+ emergency response to the East-West pipeline outage or the >$100 print was found this sweep (NOT FOUND) — nor an SPR release. Saudi cannot readily compensate for a lost export route (Al Jazeera); the August +188k bpd unwind is now irrelevant to a market short a bypass. Spare capacity is 'worn away' (Cahill). (Al Jazeera; markets.md)

recent_signals.headline: **BRENT BREAKS $100 (~$100.21 LIVE, INTRADAY SUB-$100, -3.2%); WTI ~$91 LIVE — DEAL-ANTICIPATION RE-PRICING IS NOW THE STRUCTURAL TEST FOR OPEC+ ARITHMETIC.** (1) **Mechanism**: US-Iran deal progress (senior Iranian delegation in Doha working Hormuz + frozen-asset mechanics) dumped the Hormuz tail-risk premium in the LIVE clean-room session (US Memorial Day — WTI/NYMEX frozen). If Brent closes sub-$100 for 3 sessions, Goldman's $120 Q3 base case is mathematically foreclosed and JPM's $60 2026-average case re-enters the band — a direct re-pricing of the price floor OPEC+ supply policy is managing against. (2) **Critical contradiction in the deal framework**: if Iran reopens Hormuz and the US lifts sanctions, eventual Iranian crude return to the global market is a MEDIUM-TERM bearish factor stacked on the UAE OPEC exit (effective May 1, removes ~3M+ bpd theoretical spare from cartel arithmetic — EIA cut OPEC 2027 spare-capacity forecast to 2.5M b/d from 3.8M) and forecast cuts. (3) **Saudi fiscal pressure**: break-even ~$95/bbl is now ABOVE the live Brent print — pressure on the war's primary fiscal beneficiary intensifies as Brent breaks $100. (4) **June 7 OPEC+ ministerial** remains the structural test for substantive Saudi response post-UAE-exit; with UAE out, the architecture rests on Saudi-Russia-Iraq-Kuwait. (Staleness correction: this node had not updated since May 9 — the prior Brent ~$101.73 / Goldman Q2 $90 framing is superseded.)
